title: Trump: Pentagon diverts COVID-19 funds to military contractors
description_short: Trump: Pentagon diverts COVID-19 funds to military contractors
description_medium: In April 2020, a TrumpFile timeline reported that the Pentagon used most of a $1 billion congressional COVID-19 allocation for military equipment and defense contractors. It listed surveillance technology, uniforms, body armor, and jet-engine parts. House appropriators said this conflicted with the CARES Act provision’s intent to expand protective-equipment production.
description_long: Congress allocated $1 billion to the Pentagon in 2020 for work connected to the COVID-19 response. A TrumpFile timeline reported that the department directed hundreds of millions of dollars to defense contractors for equipment it described as unrelated to the pandemic, including surveillance technology, uniforms, body armor, and jet-engine parts. It also said some funds helped defense companies stay afloat, even though some had received Paycheck Protection Program loans. At the same time, CDC Director Robert Redfield told senators that states needed $6 billion to distribute vaccines, and hospitals still faced shortages of N95 masks. The House Appropriations Committee said the Pentagon’s use of the funds ran against the CARES Act provision’s intent to spur production of personal protective equipment. The account documents a dispute over how emergency funds were spent and what Congress intended. It does not supply a full procurement breakdown, audit, or legal ruling establishing that each purchase violated the appropriation.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: Pentagon diverts COVID-19 funds to military contractors
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: Pentagon diverts COVID-19 funds to military contractors

notes: reason: The supplied timeline reports an expenditure pattern and a dispute over congressional intent but lacks the complete allocation breakdown, procurement records, and an audit or legal finding on whether the purchases were authorized.
proposed_correction: Describe the reported purchases and appropriations dispute with attribution; characterize the spending as unlawful only if an audit or court finding establishes that conclusion.

title: Trump: FBI recruits Proud Boys leader & Roger Stone ally to monitor anti-fascists
description_short: Trump: FBI recruits Proud Boys leader & Roger Stone ally to monitor anti-fascists
description_medium: A TrumpFile timeline says Proud Boys leader Joseph Biggs agreed to give the FBI information about anti-fascist activists and future Proud Boys events. The account attributes the claim to Biggs’s defense lawyer after he was charged in another case; it does not identify an FBI record confirming the meeting or its terms.
description_long: The supplied timeline says Joseph Biggs, described as a Proud Boys leader and ally of Roger Stone, met FBI agents for dinner in July 2017 and agreed to share information about anti-fascist activists and upcoming Proud Boys events. The claim came from Biggs’s defense lawyer after Biggs was charged in a separate case. That attribution matters: the timeline does not cite an FBI confirmation, court filing establishing an agreement, or details about what information Biggs provided. It also does not explain whether the FBI formally recruited him, what the agents asked him to monitor, how long any cooperation lasted, or whether the information led to action against activists. The reported dinner, if accurately described by counsel, would raise questions about the Bureau’s use of contacts inside far-right groups, but the source material does not establish the scope or reliability of the alleged arrangement. The title’s assertion that the FBI “recruits” Biggs is therefore stronger than the facts provided.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: FBI recruits Proud Boys leader & Roger Stone ally to monitor anti-fascists
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: FBI recruits Proud Boys leader & Roger Stone ally to monitor anti-fascists

notes: reason: The cooperation claim is attributed to Biggs’s defense lawyer. The supplied record identifies no FBI record or court finding confirming recruitment, the meeting’s terms, or how the information was used.
proposed_correction: Attribute the alleged dinner and offer to Biggs’s lawyer; use “recruited” only if an FBI record or court filing confirms a formal arrangement.

title: Trump: White House official involved in Ukraine scandal is promoted to the NSA
description_short: Trump: White House official involved in Ukraine scandal is promoted to the NSA
description_medium: The Pentagon appointed Michael Ellis as NSA general counsel on November 9, 2020, during the final weeks of Trump’s administration. Ellis had worked for Representative Devin Nunes and on the National Security Council, including on the Ukraine whistleblower matter. The supplied account does not establish who directed the appointment or that White House pressure caused it.
description_long: On November 9, 2020, the Pentagon named Michael Ellis general counsel of the National Security Agency. Ellis had served as counsel to Representative Devin Nunes and later worked on the National Security Council, including on the handling of the Ukraine whistleblower complaint that led to Trump’s first impeachment. The appointment drew attention because it placed a politically connected official in a senior legal role at the NSA during the administration’s final weeks. The supplied account says the White House pressured the Pentagon, but it does not identify who directed the appointment, what communications occurred, or whether that pressure determined the selection. A report about Ellis’s earlier work on the whistleblower complaint does not by itself establish that the NSA appointment was retaliation or an effort to alter intelligence work. The documented event is the appointment and Ellis’s prior roles; the motive and extent of any White House involvement remain unresolved in the available material.

preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: White House official involved in Ukraine scandal is promoted to the NSA

title: Classified Documents Theft and National Security Betrayal at Mar-a-Lago
description_short: Classified Documents Theft and National Security Betrayal at Mar-a-Lago
description_long: Donald Trump stole hundreds of classified documents including nuclear secrets, foreign intelligence, and defense information by illegally removing them to Mar-a-Lago resort while obstructing FBI investigation through systematic lies and evidence concealment that endangered national security and potentially compromised intelligence sources to foreign adversaries with access to unsecured private club. The comprehensive document theft included top secret files about nuclear weapons capabilities, foreign government intelligence, and military plans that Trump stored in ballroom, bathroom, and office spaces accessible to club members, staff, and foreign visitors who could photograph or steal America's most sensitive national security information. The national security betrayal extended to Trump's systematic obstruction of federal investigation by directing lawyers to lie about document return while moving boxes to conceal evidence from FBI search, demonstrating deliberate intent to retain classified information for personal use rather than inadvertent retention requiring cooperation with authorities. Trump's espionage-level document theft violated federal laws protecting national security by removing classified information from secure government facilities while creating opportunities for foreign intelligence services to access American secrets through Mar-a-Lago's unsecured environment that hosted foreign nationals and potential intelligence operatives. The classified documents scandal created unprecedented national security threat while demonstrating Trump's willingness to betray American intelligence interests for personal benefit, with potential exposure of intelligence sources and methods that could result in loss of human intelligence assets and compromise of ongoing national security operations. The document theft established Trump's systematic disregard for national security obligations and legal constraints, demonstrating willingness to endanger American intelligence capabilities while obstructing federal investigations through systematic deception that prioritized personal interests over protection of classified information that safeguards American lives and national defense capabilities.
subcategory: Classified Document Theft and National Security Betrayal

title: Donald Trump Jr. wants followers to storm big tech companies next
description_short: Donald Trump Jr. wants followers to storm big tech companies next
description_medium: Donald Trump Jr. shared Laura Ingraham’s call for Republicans to attend large-company shareholder meetings and ask about alleged discrimination against conservative customers. The post reached his 6.5 million followers. The proposed action was shareholder questioning; the supplied post does not call for physically storming company offices.
description_long: On January 9, 2021, Donald Trump Jr. shared a post by Fox host Laura Ingraham with his 6.5 million followers. Ingraham urged Republicans to attend shareholder meetings of large companies and ask why, in her view, those businesses discriminated against Republican customers. Trump Jr.’s post endorsed that call during a wider conservative dispute with technology companies over content moderation and political bias. The activity described was participation in corporate shareholder meetings and questioning executives, not entering company offices by force or taking over their operations. The supplied account does not identify a specific company meeting that resulted from the post, a coordinated campaign, or any change in corporate policy. The record supports a public call for shareholder activism and a large audience for the message. Its “storm big tech companies” wording exaggerates the proposed tactic and could be mistaken for a call to physical action.

preserved_fields.title: Donald Trump Jr. wants followers to storm big tech companies next
preserved_fields.description_short: Donald Trump Jr. wants followers to storm big tech companies next

notes: reason: The linked timeline quotes a call to attend shareholder meetings, not to storm company offices. It provides no evidence of a coordinated company-specific campaign or resulting action.
proposed_correction: Retitle around Trump Jr.’s endorsement of shareholder-meeting activism and keep the distinction from physical action explicit.

title: Trump: The FBI publishes ‘Wanted' posters for Russians involved in 2016 election and more
description_short: Trump: The FBI publishes ‘Wanted' posters for Russians involved in 2016 election and more
description_medium: In February 2021, the FBI began sharing wanted posters for people accused of involvement in Russian election interference. One poster named Konstantin Kilimnik, who had ties to Russian intelligence and received 2016 polling data from the Trump campaign. The FBI’s warrant against him concerned alleged obstruction of justice, not a conviction for election interference.
description_long: On February 25, 2021, the FBI began circulating wanted posters for people it accused of involvement in Russian election interference and related crimes. One named Konstantin Kilimnik, a former associate of the Trump campaign who received polling data from the campaign in 2016 and whom the FBI assessed to have ties to Russian intelligence. The poster described him as wanted for obstruction of justice and conspiracy to obstruct justice in 2018; the underlying indictment alleged that he tried to influence testimony in an official proceeding. Other FBI notices concerned Russian nationals and the Internet Research Agency, which prosecutors accused of interfering in the 2016 election. A wanted poster communicates that authorities seek a person under a warrant; it is not a conviction or a new finding about the person’s guilt. The FBI’s publication drew renewed attention to the Russian operation and to Kilimnik’s connection to campaign data, while the listed charges and allegations remained matters of legal process.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: The FBI publishes ‘Wanted' posters for Russians involved in 2016 election and more
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: The FBI publishes ‘Wanted' posters for Russians involved in 2016 election and more

notes: The linked timeline and FBI allegations distinguish the wanted notices from convictions; Kilimnik’s warrant concerned alleged obstruction, while other posters addressed the election-interference conspiracy.

title: Mass Pardon Corruption and Criminal Justice System Destruction
description_short: Mass Pardon Corruption and Criminal Justice System Destruction
description_long: Donald Trump used presidential pardon power to systematically corrupt criminal justice system by pardoning over 20 political allies convicted of fraud, tax evasion, and campaign finance violations while threatening to prosecute political enemies, creating systematic 'redefinition of crime' that protected Trump supporters while criminalizing opposition through weaponized federal law enforcement. The comprehensive pardon corruption included systematic clemency for white-collar criminals connected to Trump's circle while promising prosecution of prosecutors who had investigated Trump, effectively burning the accountability ledger and normalizing corruption through presidential protection for systematic criminal behavior. The criminal justice destruction extended to Trump's use of pardons to shield those who misused authority for personal benefit while creating new category of 'henchmen pardons' that provided license for future law-breaking by guaranteeing presidential protection for crimes serving Trump's political interests. Trump's pardon abuse violated rule of law principles by systematically protecting criminal behavior while weaponizing prosecution power against political opponents, effectively transforming justice system from equal law enforcement into political weapon that served authoritarian interests rather than constitutional accountability. The mass clemency created systematic destruction of legal accountability while demonstrating willingness to corrupt entire justice system through pardons designed to protect criminal allies while threatening prosecution of political enemies through selective law enforcement that violated equal justice principles. The pardon corruption established Trump's systematic approach to criminal justice and legal accountability, demonstrating willingness to eliminate rule of law while creating parallel justice systems where Trump supporters received protection from criminal accountability while opponents faced weaponized prosecution through systematic corruption of federal law enforcement and presidential clemency powers.
subcategory: Mass Pardon Corruption and Justice System Weaponization

title: Protest Criminalization Campaign and First Amendment Destruction
description_short: Protest Criminalization Campaign and First Amendment Destruction
description_medium: The ACLU’s analysis describes first-term National Guard deployments and federal agents’ arrests and use of force against protesters and journalists in Portland, while warning about risks under a second Trump administration. Those examples do not document a general 2025 policy criminalizing lawful protest or deporting demonstrators to El Salvador.
description_long: Donald Trump launched systematic campaign to criminalize lawful protests by threatening 'agitators will be imprisoned/or permanently sent back to country from which they came' while directing federal agencies to charge protesters with 'domestic terrorism' and threatening to send demonstrators to El Salvador prison without due process, creating unprecedented assault on First Amendment assembly rights. The comprehensive protest destruction included Trump's targeting of pro-Palestinian activists like Mahmoud Khalil, legal permanent residents married to American citizens, while systematically arresting protesters based on political viewpoint rather than criminal behavior through weaponized federal law enforcement that violated constitutional assembly protections. The First Amendment elimination extended to Trump's threats against Tesla dealership protesters while declaring intention to charge 'sick terrorist thugs' with domestic terrorism for exercising constitutional rights, demonstrating systematic willingness to criminalize political dissent through terrorism charges that eliminated peaceful protest as legitimate democratic participation. Trump's protest criminalization violated constitutional assembly rights by systematically using federal agencies to suppress political expression while transforming legitimate demonstration into terrorist activity through weaponized prosecution that served authoritarian interests rather than public safety or constitutional law enforcement. The demonstration targeting created systematic threat to democratic participation while demonstrating willingness to eliminate First Amendment protections through terrorism prosecution of peaceful protesters who challenged Trump administration policies through constitutionally protected assembly and political expression. The protest criminalization established Trump's systematic approach to political opposition and constitutional rights, demonstrating willingness to destroy First Amendment protections while using terrorism charges to eliminate peaceful dissent through federal law enforcement weaponization that transformed constitutional assembly into criminal activity deserving imprisonment or deportation rather than democratic participation protected by constitutional principles.
subcategory: Protest Criminalization and First Amendment Destruction
